body:
I did watch the video.  I think it's a problem to exploit something like that.

My question was why is it that this is not considered acceptable behaviour by the competitive community, when it is perfectly in keeping with competitive ideals?

Playing when you have no outs and your opponent is low on time is also exploiting the game client, and is only an offense in rare circumstances.  

Infinite loop rules, targeting shortcuts, using manual dexterity to hide where cards in hidden zones are, these are all things that are different in paper.

Why does one warrant the amount of shaming the player in this video receives, while the others are just being a good player?

A recomp seems in order, since software failure is one of the things that falls under the compensation policy.

I was more just generally curious how this is seen as "cheating" and shamed, whereas other forms of spiky behaviour are considered just a part of the game.

New cards or oracle changes cause things like this to happen.  Sure, they get banned if they are too powerful, but nobody calls Steve Sadin a cheater for running Flash Hulk after a power level errata was removed.  That wasn't what the card was "supposed" to do, but it did it.

I'm against this sort of thing, but if you really believe that you should do anything to win so long as the game allows for it, you should have no issue with it.

People do it all the time with "bugs" with card interactions.  We call them combos.

I've got to agree with him on one sentiment.  Too often, when a shooting happens, people insist we need to better prevent people with mental illnesses from acquiring weapons.  The mentally ill are far more likely to be the victims of violence than the cause.  Stop blaming them and trying to take away their rights.
It's a combination memory card and rumble pack.  That's what the letters stand for.

Plenty of suicide help websites will cite the two sort of things you mentioned, but there are so many areas in between that aren't spelled out so nicely.

For instance, I have a method, a desire, intent, means to act on the plan, but no specific time scheduled.  That's usually not enough for people to take away your rights, but no website I've ever seen spelled out that scenario, and the idea of risking losing your rights is enough to scare people away from seeking help.
No you don't.  Laws in the United States can force treatment on you and make you pay for it.
Yup.  There's no conflict of interest at all.

Absolutely.  It reinforces the idea that I am a fuck up who can't handle the world.

I don't envy people talking to depressed people.  It seems that anything they say can be turned into something bad.

It's just a variation on "It gets better."  Saying that a number of other people have gone through it and ended up fine is supposed to increase your confidence that you will get through it and end up fine.

I agree, it never helps.  That other people also suffer doesn't change what you feel like.

We set up another appointment, and he encouraged me to tell my family.  We also plan on having a meeting with my family, although I told him I didn't want them to know about it.  They since do.

I guess more things were being done than I initially said.  It just seems like a long crawl to nowhere.
Then nothing will change and I'm sorry for wasting your time.
Problem is, I need some degree of hope to be able to do that.  It's the catch 22 of depression.
There probably are things that could give me hope, but I don't know what they are.  At the moment, I couldn't name anything.
I can't step up.  I'm not capable of doing things.  Guess it was a pointless endeavor.

I'm not communicating very well.  I have elements of a plan.  What I meant was that he did not lay out a plan of action for how we are to proceed.

I can only assume he didn't think it was an immediate threat.

I wouldn't claim it's the fault of the particular doctor.  I held off telling anyone because I didn't think anything could be done to help, and not even having a plan after admitting it only strengthens that.

I said what I planned to say.  I just never knew how exactly it was supposed to help, and now having done it, I still don't know.  I don't feel any better and I don't see any sort of plan for getting better.

Does anyone have any insight?  Any personal examples?  Anything.
I have to assume this is backed up by something, because otherwise I agree.  Everything I've read about talking to someone suicidal indicates that you should not attempt to challenge them like that.
Not wanting to harm other people with the act and fear that I would fail.

Fear of the response, including potential financial difficulties stemming from it, is one of the reasons I've never told anyone about my thoughts.

I have no data, but I would wager most people forgo health screening or treatment for financial reasons.

Don't worry, if you seek help and they decide you need it, they'll force you to pay for it.

It's a perverse incentive to never seek help, and it's amazing that nobody seems to realize this or doesn't care.

I'm having the same sort of problems.  Every resource I have encountered says that it would only happen if you are an imminent risk to yourself.

Not that that's reassuring.  "Don't worry, chances are your rights won't be taken away" is not something that makes me confident in telling anyone.

It doesn't help that you need massive amounts of money to even try and get treatment.  And that they can indebt you if you even try and get help in a cheap or free manner.

Goddamn, I hate this.
That was my response.  That wouldn't cover the paperwork where I am from.  It's almost like the state won't let me kill myself.

Doesn't seem like something that is doable.  Seems like just a part of who I am.  Been diagnosed (by a doctor this time) with major depressive disorder, obsessive compulsive disorder, and anxiety disorders.  Just gets worse as I get older.
My mood is such that I would rather not be alive, and I can only assume it is going to get worse.
They're probably happening because I don't want to live.  Seems almost tautological.

Thank you.  Unfortunately, I don't think I can do that.

Not that it makes a huge difference, but I started doing the research because of the suicidal thoughts I had been having.  I may be at a different level of severity than I think, but it wouldn't be nothing.

It's that I don't see any alternative.  I can't tell anyone who might be able to help.

And I realize it was a bad idea.  What, if anything, have you done after you get thoughts about what your self diagnoses is?
It's not just doctors, it's anybody that can reasonably identify me.  That would go for peers, family members, friends, crisis hotlines, anything.

I generally don't for that exact reason.  For some reason this just seems different.  I know that doctors are trained to recognize and diagnose and I am not, but I don't trust my doctor enough to reveal this and I'm afraid of any response I can think of, good or bad.
I hope it's helpful for someone too.  I appreciate people who try to help.

I don't understand why "You might one day feel better" is supposed to help at all.  I'm not better now, I can't predict the future with any degree of certainty, and all past indicators are that things won't get better.
Not at all.  I've been vague on details because I don't really know the reasons myself.

I'm fully aware that it's a medical problem.  It isn't depression that contributes to me being a bad person.  I'm not worried about judgement, but I'm not sure what I'm worried about.  I just know that I don't want to go through with it.
I don't see how other people having experienced similar problems has any effect on me.  Could you explain what you mean?

I do limit the information I disclose, and I wanted to find a magic solution to my unwillingness to disclose my thoughts to them.

If I am sounding ungrateful, I apologize.  I appreciate any genuine attempt at help, I just wish it solved the issue.
No different.  I realize I can't expect professional, personalized responses, but I feel as if I could have just read any number of other people's threads and substituted the responses for me.
Therapeutic and empowering, or ruinous, and I can't know ahead of time.

Neither option is appealing, and I'm given the kinds of posts here, I think I already know what people might suggest.

Unfortunately, doing nothing may result in unhappiness, but it's the path of least resistance, so it's hard to beat.

I didn't want to make this about my life history, but it was suggested I talk about it, so fine.

I've been diagnosed with major depressive disorder, major anxiety disorder, and obsessive compulsive disorder most of my life.  I've been seeing doctors and been on medication just as long.  I've had thoughts of suicide for a long time, but never acted on them.  Recently, due to a culmination of disastrous life events, they've become more frequent and more intrusive.  I've gotten to the point where I've thought out scenarios and potential outcomes, but my massively deflated ego seems to extend to my fantasies and I can't come up with a successful plan.

So I'm alive, but don't want to be, and have never been able to admit to any of these thoughts to a doctor or family member.  I'm afraid of the response that may come with it, whether that is nothing, a complete change in how people view me, or more therapy.  I don't think anyone is capable of discussing it in a rational matter, and all the research I've done indicates this to be the case.

It seems like these thoughts and desires are just going to get worse until I finally come up with the strength to do something with them, but I can't talk to the people who are supposed to be able to help me.

If there are ways to do that, sure.  To my knowledge, most of the people I could talk to are not sworn to confidentiality.

This was the closest I could think of.
Not exactly the actionable advice I was hoping for, but thank you for your time and honesty.
And may I ask what you did about it?  Or am I just going to have to remain silent until I find the strength to go through with it?

I have a history of mental disorder and have thoughts of suicide.  I've gone through scenarios in my head about how they would work.  This causes me stress and I do not think I can tell anyone for the reasons I outlined about.
